verdict.for_whom: Action game fans willing to tolerate technical instability and connection drops should buy this, while players seeking a polished technical experience should skip it.

distortion_flags.sentence: Sentiment shifts upward after the refund window passes, moving from initial technical frustration to sustained approval despite lingering bugs.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players within the refund window encounter startup crashes, forced data collection, and sluggish melee combat.

claims.claim: The game crashes or freezes during opening cutscenes or loading screens.

citations.review_text: Crap. Gets to the start of the menu where hit says to hit a button to continue then freezes and crashes.

I have tried multiple times to delete and redownload the game, making a new save and play through the opening mission but every time, the cutscene freezes and when I click the screen, the game crashes. I WISH i was able to play this game but it literally is fighting me tooth and nail to not let me play.

Its unfortunate, I wanted to give this game a try since it looked like fun but not only does it take over 10 mins to load, when I finally get in the game it freezes and crashes when loading cutscenes.... just no... I'm refunding this.

It's a fun game, and the combat runs exceptionally smoothly at medium graphics, even on my pretty mediocre rig. Sadly, my computer just cannot handle the cutscenes, and the game consistently crashes upon any cutscene happening past the intro. 

If you have the specs to handle this game, go right on ahead, and enjoy, but I cannot continue playing this game, but this is not me speaking negatively of this game, as this is just an issue with my computer.

claims.claim: Melee and gun combat feels sluggish or weak, failing to deliver a satisfying power fantasy.

citations.review_text:
I cannot believe this poorly tutorialized, muddy, amateur mess is somehow the sequel to Space Marine, an amazing, fun, light, well designed game. Map layout frequently forgets to "hint," prompt, or nudge, making it very easy to get turned around, the tutorial frequently forgets to have the nav beacon indicate the way forward. 

The earliness and ease with which the main character is overwhelmed by swarms of low level hostiles makes this less Space Marine, and more Planetary Fodder. Yes, they have their super cool combo system where heavy attacks, parries, and executes handle fodder. Thanks for underlining how WEAK the character is that he can't chainsaw through two enemies, unlike the first game.

I think whoever made this saw Doom's melee executes and decided a few of those would carry the entire game. Ugh.

This game doesn't suffer from the original being so good that the sequel is trapped by either being boring by repetition, or missing the mark by trying to innovate and stumbling; this game suffers from being vastly less fun than the original. Some moron in design played some Soulslike and decided to ruin this game with those ideas.

I did not to play more both because the game wasn't fun and the refund window was about to close.

The audio is extremely muddled and flat. Bass is severely lacking and the mixing is atrocious on headphones. The big spooky space marine does not sound like a walking tank, and instead sounds like... nothing for the most part. Guns all sound like they have hollywood supressors on.

Controls are weightless. The gameplay loop seems to be based on a parry system with extremely misleading indicators that also take up your whole screen for some reason. I played on what was labeled the intended difficulty, and the first two hours were extremely tedious. There is no space for flare in how you can engage with enemies - you get a couple "combos" which are just RB spam chains and that's it. You bring an enemy down low enough and your guy performs a finisher. The animation pool already seemed repetitive enough after under 2 hrs. Spam - parry - finisher, maybe dodge an unparriable attack on occasion. That's all the combat has presented.

The story seems to be just bolter porn, so no interest there.

I wouldn't buy it no matter how low the discount goes.

Bought the game, played it for an hour and a half and was absolutely shocked by how terrible the actual gameplay is.

Don't get me wrong. Graphics, general sound design, voice acting etc are all top notch but that cannot save a game if the actual gameplay is boring, sluggish and NEVER manages to deliver the power fantasy that Space Marine 1 did manage to deliver. Buy that one instead as, even though it may be a bit dated graphically, it's the far superior game when it comes to the actual gameplay.

In Space Marine 2 the melee combat is sluggish, guns feel like peashooters and even grenades don't manage to put some oomph into the gameplay. 

If you want to play against large groups of bugs with exciting weapons that actually make you smile and get you into the 'oh come on one more game' groove just buy Helldivers 2 instead.

Only buy in HEAVY discount. 

The game controls are annoying. In the previous Space Marine title you had a separate button for melee attack modifier. Now you have the same button that does the regular attacks also do the special/stun attack, but it feels there is some arbitrary hold duration. So I can't ever know which attack I am charging a series/combo power attack or which I am going for a stun attack. The stupid consolified controls and UI are just a mess. 

The game scenery - the first 5 minutes you are met with not great attention to detail. They could have put more effort into polishing animations. The first big scene you see - you LITERALLY see the entities popping in out. They could have at least hidden the bugs and soldiers to have appear and dissapear behind some vision blockers. 

The character takes too much space and there is no option to edit the camera position. You are basically having a 4:3 usable screen space. Mouse movement also feels weird. Also weird scaling between aimed mode and regular viewing mode. No option for aimed sensitivity and regular sensitivity. 

Adding to that the ♥♥♥♥ that is being isntalled along with the game makes this whole thing very icky. 

And considering Saber is involved - no wonder. Seeing how they did Quake Champions it is no surprise how this ended up. The moment I saw the trailers of items moving in space with misaligned movement and direction, as well as the lighting, I guessed Saber is involved without even researching into it. The Swarm Engine is basically Saber3D that was used for Quake Champions and which crashed it to the ground. So again no warm feelings for Saber. 

Really not impressed and not for this kind of money. I really HATE how modern game development is just doing consoles first and BARELY any effort for the PC port and its controlls. And Saber is involved, so more minus points. 

TLDR: This is yet another money grab console port that is primarily a platform for DLC sale with something like a simpli…

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players navigate linear levels and a brief campaign while dealing with animation locks and multiplayer crashes.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that levels are designed as narrow, linear corridors from point A to point B.

citations.review_text:
I am new to the W40k universe, so with that in mind...

THE GOOD
Visuals
Gory finishers
Lore and story - as far as I can tell
Multiple game modes to enjoy - Campaign, PvE missions, challenges, PVP
Enjoyable co-op

THE WEIRD
The game didn't wanna run at stable 1080p 60 fps on my rig in large empty interiors but ran 60 stable with hundreds of enemies on the screen so I had to use DLSS+framegen to make it smooth.
Early mission sections sometimes transport you into a new place without an obvious transition.

THE BAD
85% of the levels are just S-shaped corridors going into another S-shaped corridor, which can be hard to navigate especially in the jungle or the factory setting, since every building in this universe is so large.
The small rat-sized enemies are super clunky
The menus can be pretty slow since the game is made to allow a quick drop-in and drop-out of other players.

SUMMARY
SM2 is a great action game, a must-have if you enjoy the universe or want a new co-op game to grind through with up to 2 of your friends.

If you just want to enjoy all of the meat solo like myself, it can be somewhat lacking so consider getting it on a discount and see if you like it. 

I have enjoyed it a lot, I just wish there was more unique stuff to explore and fight.

This was my first time playing a warhammer 40k game after becoming addicted to listening to lore videos on youtube. I was hoping to get an immersive experience of the Grim Dark universe, but everything feels really washed down and sterile. This game should be a dystopian horror game, like Quake 4 was, showing unimaginable human suffering and despair. Instead you just kill tyrannids over and over again and don't get to see much about life and culture within the Imperium or Xenos. 

The gameplay feels braindead, with a clunky Hack and Slash mechanic where you are constantly fishing for animations that restore your shields. In other words, it feels like you are playing mostly for quick-time events. Normal difficulty was laughably easy so I swapped to Veteran and the only real skill check is how much you spam those quick time event animations to heal yourself. 

There is no skill tree and hardly any gear customization options. There is no exploration aside from finding a bit of ammo or health packs on the side of the path. You are just constantly walking through a very narrow main path. Gameplay wise, it is appropriate for kids, but probably understimulating even to the average teenager these days. For a game rated 18+ I would expect more complexity and tactical depth.

claims.claim: Combat involves animation locks during parries and melee actions.

citations.review_text: Do you enjoy being animation locked every 5 secs? The game is fine but the combat is so bad you'll stop playing after a few hours, to block or parry it locks you in an animation. Compared to Darktide, Vermintide or even Gears of War the melee combat in this game is truly bad and the number 1 reason why people don't play. All other games have freedom of movement , it's not fun to be locked , truly disappointing. Can't even jump. No bullet decals ,some objects don't even register phsical hits.

A lot of people like the game, thats cool a lot of people like to smoke crack and groom kids too that doesnt make it good. Combat just sucks, it wants to demand you get good at it but it doesnt have the decency to be fun enough to want to. Your sword has no weight, your gun shoots BB's and your character feels like hes moving under water. Animation locks galore as you swing your cardboard sword and dozens of enemies chip away at you with guns from across the screen while youre stuck perma dodging the 40 zerglings that threaten to evaporate your whole health bar should you stop dodge roll spamming. Its a spectacle and WH is a cool universe but the execution here is bad. Some people, mega fans of WH might like it but theres a reason this game lives on a deep discount to barely maintain its tiny player base. Most people will not enjoy horde shooter dark souls aka SM II

claims.claim: Reviewers experience persistent multiplayer disconnection issues that cause them to lose earned progress and experience near the end of operations.

citations.review_text:
Game keeps disconnecting from servers on multiplayer, I have tried all fixes that I could find to no avail.
there are better days when I am getting maybe one or two and there are others when it is impossible to play a match in full.
Game itself is engaging, fun to play and learning curve is steep but rewarding, I wish story (single player) was a bit longer. 
there is also a bit too much loading screens for my taste.
All in all if disconnection issues are solved this will be really good game, but for now it is a bit disappointing to play and be disconnected near the end of operation etc.

I love this game, but it has a few problems. The missions are too long and at least once a play session, I get disconnected in the middle of the mission or near the end even and all the experience and credits I would earn are completely lost due to no fault of mine. It's exhausting and I can't do it any more. Thanks but no thanks.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from launch and startup crashes that require troubleshooting before playing.

citations.review_text: You have to spend 30-60 minutes every time you want to play to figure out 5 different reasons why it keeps crashing on laucnh this time. I spent more time reading forum posts than playing the game. Once it launches its fine. I dont know if its the easy anti cheat or what, but this should not be acceptible for a 2 year old game in 2026, especially since MANY people seem to have the same issue and is nowhere adressed by the company it seems.

Holy moly moly holy, I absolutely loved this game, and have found only 2 issues with it in my whole time playing. So, I had wanted to buy this game for a long time, and had no idea that I would get so incredibly hooked. The gameplay loop is insanely satisfying, taking on hordes of enemies hundreds and thousands at a time is incredible. The story is adrenaline pumped directly into the veins, with the most testosterone fueled ending mission i've ever played. Customisation and operation missions that run concurrently with the main campaign is where I sunk most of my hours, and I have no regrets. If you love horde fighting games and large scale battle games, buy this immediately when on sale. Now for the issues, two fairly significant ones. Firstly, the PVP modes are some of the worst things i've ever seen, with insanely imbalanced skill levels amongst matchmaking, the slowest servers of all time, mostly due to no interest at all in those servers, and essentially what can be decribed as grenade spam and overstimulation, which is a crazy statement considering the amount of particle affects that occur during the main story. Another issue is the Alt+tab phenomenon, which only occurred in my last 10-12 hours of playtime, which is perhaps the most infuriating thing of all time. You will tab out, the game freezes, and then crashes. It is genuinely a major issue that is WELL KNOWN, so to fix it I recommend turning off Hardware accelerated Gpu Scheduling. ANYWHO, amazing game that is easily in my top five, just with a couple of issues that aren't even central to the game and shouldn't occur for most players, would definitely recommend to those players I previously mentioned. BUY IT FOR THE EMPEROR OR DIE!

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the parry and blocking mechanics have a strict learning curve and are unforgiving.

citations.review_text:
Massively overrated with some of the most inconsistent, contradictory, frustrating game design I've ever experienced. 

The audio-visual design is trash and makes combat an absolutely unreadable cluster, with multiple systems competing for your attention (dodge and parry cues sharing the same audio indicator is a particularly egregious sin); the gameplay tries to chase that "deliberate and measured" trend from "soulslike" games combined with character-action horde combat, which just results in a clunky game where you're easily overwhelmed; game mechanics are littered with exceptions and inconsistencies, particularly with enemy attacks and the parry system; the control schemes available are all generally awkward and awful no matter which of the limited options you pick (none of them do a good job combining both melee and gun combat while allowing easy use of abilities, there's always a trade-off); the general UI is convoluted, makes party management awkward and needlessly hides various screens; pointless loading screens that shouldn't exist (I shouldn't have to reload the hangar when leaving a party!); an upgrade system that is often confusing and somewhat of a slog; the list goes on and on and on.....

I tried to like it, I really did, but in the end the experience keeps pissing me off. Makes Darktide look competent by comparison, which is saying a lot.

I had no history on anything Warhammer related going into this and just thought it'd be like Vermintide 2, which I liked. BOY WAS I IN FOR A TREAT.. This game is simply FANTASTIC! The movement, combat and ESPEICALLY the world building is so well thought out and implemented. Not only that but the combat is extremely challenging on harder difficulties and is pretty much like a souls-like game where you have to know your combos or else you'll get downed. 
Other great highlights include the extremely detailed armor customization and being able to adjust both your perks and weapon upgrades for exactly the type of playstyle you like. I also cannot believe how stable this game is online, from all the times that I've been playing co-op or in random match-making lobbies has the game crashed once in the 40 hours I have currently put in. 
Yeah, great game!

Loving the coop gameplay and difficulty variation you're able to do with players and how populated each difficulty is with coop. Will go ahead and let anyone who is going to play, the parry and blocking aspect of the game is not forgivable at all and i recommend watching a couple tutorials and also experimenting with it before thinking you know what each one means. they don't mean what you think they mean. Overall the game has been super fun, interesting and takes alot of time to progress everything so its not a 10hour game and youre maxxed out which i love about it.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Veterans face punishing endgame content, balancing complaints in player-versus-player modes, cosmetic lock requirements, and persistent mission bugs.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that PvP mode suffers from poor balancing, with certain weapons consistently outperforming others and mechanics that favor specific classes or coordinated teams over random players.

citations.review_text:
The PvE was never particularly good for anything other than the cinematic/hype value of it - I would always recommend Darktide if you're interested in a 40k horde shooter over SM2, as well as older games like Vermintide 2 if you don't care about the 40k setting in particular and just want the gameplay.

PvP was very fun when the game launched, but the devs have since heavily prioritized the PvE portion of the game and of course the DLC cosmetics.

This wild west yolo approach to PvP balance can only work for so long, and now everyone knows how to exploit all the broken systems that Saber refuses to invest dev time into addressing. Every deathmatch round devolves into spawn locking by a firing squad that needs levels of teamwork that cannot be expected of randoms to break, every take and hold match is heavies with meltas sitting on points outside any enemy line of fire farming melee specialists that thought getting to walk into melee range of a ranged support class was a good idea, etc etc. Given the current state of the game, melee combat is near worthless in PvP, and the only truly useful melee class is the Bulwark - which has nothing at all to do with it being melee and everything to do with it's special ability being a powerful force multiplier for blob fights as well as the shield making them immune to shooting. Assault is genuinely useless on half the new maps - it's only saving grace is the fact that gamers don't look up so you can put extra shooting pressure (or set up a dive with the hammer) on a target from above if you launch yourself upwards from out of line of sight and then glide around a corner. Even on favorable maps where you can use the jetpack to reposition quickly, shooting down the squishy 2 armor assault is trivial - in fact if your 1v1 solution to anything Assault does is just 'aim gun at the assault and hold down left click' you will win 90% of the time as long as you are capable of looking up. Even Vanguards who are ostensibly built to co…

PVE is great. Special weapons with perks and abilities keep the gameplay fun and engaging. You are an instrument of the Emperor's divine wrath mowing down his enemies in a tide of blood and gore. The enemies pose a significant challenge where strategy and teamwork must be used. PVP is another story. 

In PVP, the balancing is just, bad. It seems there are just a few weapons that always outperform the others even when they have a tactical disadvantage. Example: a heavy at close range with a multi-melta should dominate whoever is in range. However, the heavy-bolter still outperforms even in this situation. Armor needs a serious buff. The deaths happen so quickly, there seems to be almost no point in having a sidearm either. An epic battle between Space Marines in power armor should last a little bit longer. It makes sense for melee to be fast paced and sudden, the ranged damage not so much. 

All in all, great game worth every penny. Hopefully they can make the PVP battles feel more epic and engaging. Brother versus traitorous brother. 

The Emperor protects.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe high-difficulty endgame and absolute difficulty content as punishing and frustrating due to persistent bugs, balancing issues, and heavy reliance on ranged enemy spam.

citations.review_text:
I love this game. The combat is addicting, and the visual design really gives you the FEEL of what it's like to be a Space Marine in Warhammer 40k. Learning how to handle every enemy, or how to use every class and every weapon, is a deeply enjoyable process. (At least, for me it was.) And for most players, that's probably enough.

However.

Unless you are a player that enjoys challenge, or is something of a glutton for punishment, I do not recommend players approach the endgame content in its current state. Play up to Ruthless or Lethal difficulty, and you'll have a good time. But if you don't enjoy difficulty for the sake of overcoming challenge, do not go higher than Lethal. Normal siege is fine, and normal stratagems are fine, but I do not recommend Hard Strats or Hard siege OR ABSOLUTE in its current state.

Here's why.

I have roughly 1100, closing in on 1200 hours in this game. I can true solo Absolute difficulty (the hardest difficulty) with multiple classes, and I can sometimes carry in Hard Stratagems (Endgame content). And unfortunately the truth is that this game still has some bugs and balancing issues to work out. So I would warn any casual players away from the harder content simply because in the game's current state, unless you enjoy learning how to handle punishing difficulty in games, you're going to have an experience that feels entirely unfair.

It's not that the hardest difficulties or endgame content is unbeatable - far from it. With the right strategies, builds, and approach to combat, all of the hardest missions in the PVE can be cleared. However, learning how to make the most of all the weapons and perks at your disposal can take an absurd amount of time and it's not something you simply try once or twice and suddenly understand - it takes hours and sometimes days for you to ACTUALLY master these things. It is a serious time commitment.

So at the end of the day, yes, I recommend this game. But for the casual player I recommend you play it a…

At its core, the game is absolutely amazing. Gunplay is awesome, melee combat is amazing, and customisation is absolute peak.

But the game suffers from enemy cheese. Ranged spam is insane. You will get shot at from every possible side of the map. If you play against Tyranids, expect to drown in spore mines, barbed ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bushes or whatever they are, snipers, and every possible ranged enemy they can come up with. Chaos is a bit better, but there are, of course, Terminators who will drown you in rocket spam, which has no problem going around cover. They also have miniguns with, as it seems, very low damage drop-off and will absolutely refuse to engage in melee.

And, well, we have a siege mode, which, as it stands now, will not grant us accolade points. So we need to suffer through all the ranged ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for no reward. I mean, I am winning games, but even those feel like losses lately.

This game could so easily be so much better.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that recent updates tied certain unlockable cosmetics to PvP-mode challenges, which frustrates players who prefer to focus exclusively on PvE content.

citations.review_text:
Great Game. Really love it and will continue to play it. Best PvE Hordeshooter out there, with one of the best lores behind it.

Reason for downvote is simple. I play this game for the PvE-part (as most people do) and with the new patch, they added cosmetics that are only unlockable if you play PvP-mode. I get that they try to promote their dead PvP-Gamemode, but i don't want to be forced to play a gamemode i don't like, just to unlock the cosmetics i want.

I have more than enough time in this game to say its well worth playing and i encourage anyone on the fence to do so but if I'm going to be completely honest, locking PVE cosmetics behind PVP challenges is a sure fire way to make me not want to play any of that content. A simple "this or that" challenge would have been an easy fix to make it accessible to all play types instead of trying to push people into modes they just don't enjoy.

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter various technical issues and bugs during missions, including broken contested health mechanics, unresponsive parries, and mechanics failing to function properly.

citations.review_text:
I understand I have just over 1,000 hours in this game.  I will continue to put hours into it, because this is the modern Space Marine faction game we got whether I like it or not.

However, I must make known my issue I take with this game: it just never functions as it should.  *Ever*.  If Contested Health doesn't break and inexplicably stop working at random points during a mission, my perks take their place.  If that works, then an enemy spawn effect kills me from 10 meters away.  If that doesn't happen, my medicae stim fails to heal me.  If that works, my parries are ignored completely.  And if that works, my dodges manage to simultaneously succeed *and* fail, as I get the sound and visual cue for a perfect dodge, and yet get staggered and hurt regardless(these are not including specific modifiers that do some of these things, obviously; I have experienced all of the above separately in regular missions on the hardest difficulty, where I am otherwise comfortable).

I genuinely hope the third game they are working on redeems them.  I want them to prove they can make something that works as it should, at the very least.  But if they can't, I hope it is an utter embarrassment for them in all senses of the term, as I fully believe they should not be at this wheel they have found themselves behind.

P.S. Whatever happens, do not allow these developers to forget that they broke one of the main weapon defense types - turning off its AOE damage and stagger, half of the allure of this defense type, *by accident* somehow - and didn't fix it until two patches later, all while the community made a patch for it in less than a month after it was found(the issue was literally a toggle in the game's files).

The developers have known about this bug for over a month, yet it still hasn't been fixed or meaningfully addressed in any patch.

Even worse, despite knowing the modifier was broken, they included it in a high-reward weekly mission that they manually curate themselves.

There has been no official acknowledgement, no temporary workaround, and no explanation to the community.

From a player's perspective, this doesn't look like a simple mistake anymore. It looks like the developers are ignoring their own players and treating serious gameplay issues as a low priority.
allways quality assurance, bug fixing, and communication are simply unacceptable for a live-service game.
